subject: BetaCore pilot: retainer vs performance-credit structuring
messages:
From: Alex Zhao <alex.zhao@betacore.ai>
To: Sean Gallagher <sean.gallagher@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
Date: 2025-08-14T10:23:00-07:00
Subject: Pilot pricing structure - Betacore x Redwood

Hi Sean / Marissa,

Thanks again for the demo yesterday — the latency and cost breakdown looked promising for our search-summarization use case. Procurement asked me to put two pilot pricing options on the table so we can evaluate which aligns with internal forecasting:

Option A — Fixed monthly retainer (time-boxed pilot):
- 30-day pilot at $25,000 (fixed)
- Includes up to 10M inference tokens and 8 hours of allocated engineering time for integration and triage
- Option to extend for additional 15 days at $12,500

Option B — Performance credits (usage-backed):
- No retainer; billed as credits at $5 per 1k inference tokens used during pilot
- Includes 4 hours of integration time (additional hours billable)
- If we hit >12M tokens, BetaCore requests a 20% discount on credit rate for tokens above that threshold

We are open to hybrid approaches but procurement prefers predictability. I've attached our short requirements doc (Betacore_POC_requirements.pdf).

Could you confirm which option fits Redwood's recommended pilot packaging and whether there are standard concessions you typically include for a company at our stage? Also please share the simplest legal/PO flow — procurement is asking about caps and CD/SoW before we proceed.

Best,
Alex
Product Partnerships
BetaCore AI

Attachment: Betacore_POC_requirements.pdf (application/pdf)

From: Sean Gallagher <sean.gallagher@redwood.ai>
To: Alex Zhao <alex.zhao@betacore.ai>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
Date: 2025-08-14T12:08:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Pilot pricing structure - Betacore x Redwood

Alex — thanks for laying this out and for the clear requirements doc. Quick read-through thoughts (high level):

- Both options are reasonable; each maps to different risk profiles.
- For sales motion and engineering runway we typically recommend a time-boxed retainer for first integrations (Option A) because it guarantees dedicated capacity and a small engineering SLA. It also makes success metrics easier to align on.

Suggested hybrid we’ve used before: Monthly retainer (smaller) + performance credit top-up. Example:
- 30-day pilot: $18,000 retainer (includes up to 7.5M tokens + 6 engineering hours)
- Performance credits: $4/1k tokens above included amount
- If BetaCore consumes >12M tokens in 30 days, we trigger an automatic review and can apply a 15% volume discount for the overage bucket

Two asks from our side:
1) Confirm the primary pilot success metric (e.g., 95th percentile response latency < 600ms; or accuracy threshold on 2k eval prompts) so we can scope the engineering hours.
2) Confirm who from procurement/legal will own the PO flow so we can send a tailored SOW and speed up signature.

If BetaCore is firmly budgeted for a fixed retainer, we can adopt option A as-is; the hybrid above is often a middle ground that keeps forecastability while protecting Redwood for heavy bursts.

Happy to jump on a quick 30-min call. What does your availability look like tomorrow (Aug 15)?

—Sean
Head of Sales, Redwood Inference

From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
To: Alex Zhao <alex.zhao@betacore.ai>, Sean Gallagher <sean.gallagher@redwood.ai>
Cc: David Kim <david.kim@redwood.ai>, Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.ai>
Date: 2025-08-14T14:35:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Pilot pricing structure - Betacore x Redwood

Alex + Sean — quick follow from my side with an ops perspective. I put together a short matrix that maps pilot packaging to operational commitments (see attached).

Key clarifications: 
- Engineering hours: we track these in 30-min blocks; any integration over the included hours will be billed at our standard hourly rate (listed in the attachment).
- Data retention & logs: for pilots we retain logs for 30 days by default; if you need longer retention for evaluation we can configure 90 days but that adds to cost.
- SLA/uptime: we offer a commercial SLA only on Dedicated trials; hosted pilots get best-effort SLOs and incident reporting.

Alternative suggestion: graduated credit ladder — start with a smaller retainer and increase the credit discount as you hit milestones (e.g., 0–6M tokens no discount, 6–12M 10% discount, >12M 15% discount). This preserves budget predictability while giving BetaCore upside on volume.

Please see redwood_pilot_pricing_matrix.xlsx for line items.

—Marissa
Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
Attachment: redwood_pilot_pricing_matrix.xlsx (application/vnd.openxmlformats-officedocument.spreadsheetml.sheet)

From: Laura Chen <laura.chen@betacore.ai>
To: Sean Gallagher <sean.gallagher@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
Cc: procurement@betacore.ai
Date: 2025-08-15T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Pilot pricing structure - Betacore x Redwood

Thanks Sean / Marissa — procurement here (Laura). A couple of constraints from our side: 

- Budget: we have a single-line pilot budget and prefer fixed retainer pricing for forecasting. Our finance lead needs a firm cap.
- Deliverables: we need the SOW to enumerate integration deliverables (connector, sample prompt set evaluation, one handover session).
- Payment terms: Net30 is preferred; we will sign a short SOW + PO rather than DocuSign for the first run if you can accommodate.

Given that, our internal ask is: would Redwood accept a 30-day fixed retainer at $25k with the following: 10M included tokens, 6 engineering hours, and an explicit milestone (handover checklist) that must be met for an optional 15-day extension at $12,500? If so, we can route PO and have procurement/legal send the formal request.

If you need a cap on liability or a minimal amendment to the SOW we can include standard procurement terms. We do not want overcomplicated tiered credits for this first evaluation.

Thanks,
Laura Chen
Head of Procurement, BetaCore AI

From: Sean Gallagher <sean.gallagher@redwood.ai>
To: Laura Chen <laura.chen@betacore.ai>, Alex Zhao <alex.zhao@betacore.ai>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, David Kim <david.kim@redwood.ai>, Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.ai>
Date: 2025-08-15T16:02:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Pilot pricing structure - Betacore x Redwood

Laura — appreciate the clarity. We can accept the fixed-retainer path for the first pilot with the terms you outlined. Quick confirmations and next steps: 

Confirmed proposal (final):
- 30-day fixed retainer: $25,000 (includes up to 10M inference tokens + 6 engineering hours)
- Optional 15-day extension: $12,500 if handover checklist completed and both parties agree
- Payment: Net30 via PO (we can accept a PO and attach a short SOW; DocuSign link also available if you prefer a signature flow)
- Data retention: default 30 days (option to extend to 90 days by mutual agreement)
- If BetaCore consumes >12M tokens during the 30-day window we will notify procurement and propose a discounted overage pricing; we will not auto-bill beyond the included cap without explicit approval

Action items:
1) Laura/procurement: please route PO to finance@redwood.ai with reference DEAL-987 and include the SOW checklist items (connector, prompt eval, handover session).
2) Sean/Marissa: I will prepare a 1-page SOW and send it to the HubSpot deal and to Laura for review.
3) David Kim (cc): please confirm the PO receiving address and any required invoice fields for Net30 processing.

Links: HubSpot deal: https://app.hubspot.com/contacts/1234567/deal/DEAL-987
DocuSign (optional): https://www.docusign.com/sign/abc123-pilot-agreement

If that's all aligned I'll draft the SOW and send it by EOD tomorrow so procurement can attach the PO. Thanks everyone — looking forward to running this with BetaCore.

—Sean
